title: Give no more than a fifth, and start at six
summary: Why a person who incurs a greater punishment doesn't also pay damages, Yaakov's fear for Binyamin and the teaching that everything is in Heaven's hands except cold and heat, and how the four deaths of beis din still come after the Churban. The warning against going about as a gossip and guarding one's thoughts by day, a husband's obligations to his wife, and the father who will not support his children. Then the takanah of Usha not to give more than a fifth to tzedakah, and Rav's instruction to take a child into the class from six and "stuff him like an ox."
